nota: Archived NASA data, downloaded on 2026-11-14. Daily dose = mean of hourly absorbed_dose_rate from LRO/CRaTER-D1D2 (lunar orbit). Level: below 8 = 0, 8-50 = 1, 50-500 = 2, above 500 = 3.

fontes.nome: LRO / CRaTER radiation dose, via NASA OSDR RadLab

dias.aviso: Good morning, Commander! At 06:01 UTC the Sun fired an X1.3 flare from sunspot region 13663. A flare is a flash of light and X-rays. Radiation near the Moon is calm today.
dias.fato: Flares are ranked A, B, C, M and X. X is the strongest. Light from the Sun reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes.

dias.aviso: Big flash! An X4.5 flare at 06:35 UTC. The fast particles that harm astronauts have not arrived. Radiation is still calm.
dias.fato: Sunspots are darker, cooler areas on the Sun with strong magnetic fields. Most big flares start there.

dias.aviso: A quieter day: only M-class flares (M5.1 and M8.2). Radiation is calm. A good day to work on the rocket!
dias.fato: The Moon has no thick air and no global magnetic field. On Earth, both help block radiation from space.

dias.aviso: Watch out: three X1.0 flares today. At 22:24 UTC the Sun threw a cloud of solar material into space at 1,257 km/s. It is called a CME. Radiation is still calm, but a storm is coming.
dias.fato: A CME (coronal mass ejection) is a giant cloud of gas and magnetic field thrown out by the Sun. It crosses to the Moon in one to three days.

dias.aviso: Storm alert! An X2.2 flare at 09:13 UTC. At 13:59 UTC NASA detected fast particles from the Sun. Radiation is RISING.
dias.fato: Solar energetic particles are very fast protons. Thin walls do not stop them, so a base needs radiation shielding.

dias.aviso: Big storm! An X3.9 flare at 06:54 UTC and more fast particles from 12:59 UTC. On Earth, a Kp 9 geomagnetic storm starts at 15:00 UTC, the strongest in more than 20 years. Radiation is HIGH.
dias.fato: On Earth this storm made auroras far from the poles. Earth's magnetic field protected people there. The Moon has no such shield.

dias.aviso: EXTREME! An X5.8 flare at 01:23 UTC. This is the highest radiation of the mission. Protect the crew!
dias.fato: µGy/h (micrograys per hour) measures how much radiation energy a body absorbs each hour.

dias.aviso: The storm is fading, but radiation is still HIGH. Today is launch day: the rocket must be ready tonight!
dias.fato: NASA's Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office watches the Sun every day and logs events in DONKI, the database this game uses.
